a.displayName: Working Olive (every drawn area and its lines)

picture-green.source: Baked into both map pictures by their build scripts; not a --th-* role.

picture-sand.source: Baked into the four public/landing/town-*.svg pictures by scripts/build-hero-town.mjs; not a --th-* role.

picture-building.source: Baked into the four public/landing/town-*.svg pictures by scripts/build-hero-town.mjs; not a --th-* role.

picture-built.source: Baked into public/landing/island.svg by scripts/build-island-map.mjs; not a --th-* role.

picture-road-minor.source: Baked into the four public/landing/town-*.svg pictures by scripts/build-hero-town.mjs; not a --th-* role.

picture-road-secondary.source: Baked into public/landing/island.svg by scripts/build-island-map.mjs; not a --th-* role.

picture-road.source: Baked into both map pictures by their build scripts; not a --th-* role.

picture-motorway.source: Baked into public/landing/island.svg by scripts/build-island-map.mjs; not a --th-* role.

rail.source: --hw-rail, local to .hw-line in app/landing-how.css: color-mix(in srgb, var(--th-a) 70%, var(--th-ground)). Not yet a --th-* role.

display.purpose: The first screen's headline only, in three lines. clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 3.5rem) below 1024px; line-height 1.04 throughout.

headline.purpose: The stage's heading, the heading of How the numbers are made and the close's heading (--th-heading); line-height 1.08 on the close.

card-name.purpose: A product's name in its card's 56px header row: the headline size times 0.7.

wordmark.purpose: The name beside the brand mark in the nav; 18px in the footer.

title.purpose: A product's name in a stage panel and a stop's name on the How line; weight 700 for a report page's title.

lede.purpose: The one muted sentence under a heading; 18px from 640px. The first screen's is a size up: 18px on phones, 20px from 1024px. The search field's own text is 17px in ink.

body.purpose: The report page, the conversation (17px from 640px) and form input.

body-small.purpose: Notes, panel text, the stage's messages, list rows, a row of the place list, what a stop on the How line says.

figure.purpose: A number, tabular, followed by its unit at 13px in muted. On a card pinned on the first screen's picture the figures are a small table at 13px/20px: count and figure in ink at weight 600, their words in muted.

action.purpose: Buttons, text links, switch options, the Draw an area here button; tabs and nav links at weight 500.

caption.purpose: What a figure block covers, chart captions, notes under controls, what kind of place a row is. Muted.

micro.purpose: Place names on a map (haloed), chart axis ticks at weight 400, the map credit and the tour's pause control, the sample and example-listing notes.

shadows.name: shadow-color
shadows.purpose: --th-shadow: the one shadow colour, ink at 35%.

shadows.name: sheet-on-card
shadows.purpose: The report sheet lying on the Reports card. Shortens to 0 14px 22px -16px and 0 10px 16px -12px in short windows.

shadows.name: sheet-in-panel
shadows.purpose: The sample report page in the stage's Reports panel.

shadows.name: pinned-to-map
shadows.purpose: An area's card on the first screen's picture, pinned beside its area or docked in the band's corner while the band is on that area. The card also has a 1px ink edge. It is a three-line table: short-let, long-let and for sale, each with its count and median.

shadows.name: floating-control
shadows.purpose: The zoom control on the stage map's top-right corner and the Draw an area here button on its bottom-left.

shadows.name: listing-card
shadows.purpose: The example listing's card at the first stop of the How line.

shadows.name: way-in
shadows.value: 0 2px 3px -1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--th-ink) 24%, transparent), 0 20px 32px -18px color-mix(in srgb, var(--th-ink) 50%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: The glass search field on the first screen: a contact shadow and a deep one, with the light the glass gathers set in the middle of the deep one.

shadows.name: way-in-list
shadows.purpose: The frosted glass list of places open under the search field.

shadows.name: knock-out-ring
shadows.purpose: Around a chart's hover dot so it reads off the line.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: --th-ease: the one easing, for every transform and every authored moment.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Fill and colour changes on hover, and the 0.97 press.

motion.name: nudge
motion.purpose: An arrow moving 3px, an underline dropping from 4px to 7px.

motion.name: open
motion.purpose: A stage panel growing open and its chevron turning.

motion.name: first-screen-tour
motion.value: first town complete for 3.6s; then per town: map slides in 3% over 1.2s (opacity 0.9s ease), dots from 0.4s west to east, drawing from 1.1s at 0.17s a corner (corner th-drop 0.35s, line th-trace linear), area sets on closing (tint 0.3s, card opacity 0.3s and translate 6px 0.4s, both after 0.15s) and stays 1.1s to be read (1.7s in the band), 0.5s to the next area, hold 2.2s, leave 0.45s; in the band the map pans 0.7s and the docked card goes as it moves
motion.purpose: The first screen's picture, which runs by itself and loops through six towns. It waits while out of view, while the tab is hidden and while the visitor types in the search field, and can be paused. With reduced motion the first town stays, complete, and there is no pause control.

motion.name: stage-intro
motion.value: handles drop 0.5s (90ms stagger), outline traces 0.75s at 0.55s, fill fades at 1s, wires trace at 1.5s and 1.7s
motion.purpose: The stage's one moment on first load.

motion.name: corner-cue
motion.purpose: One handle sends out a slow ring until a corner is first moved. Under reduced motion the corner is filled olive instead.

motion.name: card-arrival
motion.value: chart wipe 0.9s, node pop 0.3s, bars grow 0.4s, sheet dealt 0.5s, message arrives 0.45s
motion.purpose: What plays once when a card is first well into view. Everything is in its final state without it.

motion.name: covered-card
motion.value: scale(0.97) and a 6% ink veil on animation-timeline: view()
motion.purpose: A pinned card's body recedes as the next card comes over it; its header row does not.

motion.name: picture-fade
motion.value: mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0, #000 24%), linear-gradient(180deg, transparent 0, #000 15%), linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0, #000 6%), intersected; below 1024px linear-gradient(180deg, transparent 0, #000 16%)
motion.purpose: Not motion: how the first screen's frameless picture meets the paper. On the drawing alone; what is drawn over it does not fade.

breakpoints.name: search-button-words
breakpoints.value: (max-width: 479px), (min-width: 1024px) and (max-width: 1179px): the search button is its arrow alone

breakpoints.name: nav
breakpoints.value: 768px (the nav's links fold into a menu below it)

breakpoints.name: how-line
breakpoints.value: 1100px (the How line runs left to right from here)

components.name: Close Field and Paper Button
components.description: The email field and its submit on the ink close: the palette turned over.
components.css: .ds-close { font-family: var(--th-font, 'Google Sans', sans-serif); display: flex; gap: 10px; padding: 24px; background: var(--th-close, #161C11); } .ds-close-input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1.5px solid var(--th-close-edge, #7C7E74); border-radius: 12px; background: transparent; color: var(--th-close-ink, #F4F1E8); font: inherit; font-size: 16px; caret-color: var(--th-close-ink, #F4F1E8); transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-close-input::placeholder { color: var(--th-close-muted, #BABAB0); opacity: 1; } .ds-close-input:hover, .ds-close-input:focus { border-color: var(--th-close-ink, #F4F1E8); } .ds-close-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--th-close-ink, #F4F1E8); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-paper { font-family: inherit; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; min-width: 120px; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 22px; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, transform 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); background: var(--th-close-ink, #F4F1E8); color: var(--th-close, #161C11); } .ds-btn-paper:hover { background-color: var(--th-surface, #FFFFFF); } .ds-btn-paper:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-paper:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--th-close-ink, #F4F1E8); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-paper svg { transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-paper:hover svg { transform: translateX(3px); }

components.name: Switch
components.description: Options in a white tray; the chosen one is solid ink. Used once, for the kind of report at the head of the Reports card's contents.

components.name: Map Controls
components.description: What floats on the stage's map: plus over minus on one white surface, Whole island under them once the map is zoomed, and Draw an area here whenever the map is zoomed in or no part of the area is in the window.

components.name: Square Corners

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Drawn Area"**

The whole page is drawn with the tool the product hands the visitor: an area with an olive outline and square white corners you can pick up. The brand mark is that area with five square handles. The first screen shows them being drawn: a tour of six drawn town maps that runs by itself, three areas a few streets wide on each, every one answered on a small white card with how full its short-lets are and what a night costs, next to a search field that asks the visitor for their own place. The second screen, the stage, is one map of the island that zooms, with one such area on it whose corners drag, joined by thin lines to three product panels. The product icons, the chart ends, the report's contents rail, the chosen question, the slider's handle and the five stops of "How the numbers are made" are all the same square corner. Nothing on the page is illustrated in another hand.

The ground is a warm beige on every screen and nearly everything on it is ink. Two colours carry meaning and they do not trade jobs: olive works (every drawn area, its outline and its lines, the one filled action, the visitor's own words) and a light orange marks (the brand mark, the three product icons, the listing that is being counted, a booked night, and in four steps how full each listing has been). The map pictures (six towns and the island) are generated from OpenStreetMap data in the page's own quiet map colours; they carry no labels of their own and no boundary lines, they are credited on the page, and what names appear on them are set by the page in its own type. The page ends by turning the palette over: paper on ink, for the close and the footer only.

Density rises as the visitor goes down. The first screen holds a headline, one sentence, one field and one picture. The stage and the cards are working instruments set in small, exact type with tabular figures. The system is flat: hairlines divide, and a shadow appears only under something that lies on top of something else.

Confirmed rejections: teal and tangerine are both out of the palette; a dark first screen was built and rejected by the owner, and the ground stays beige; the page must not read as AI-generated (no pill or badge labels, no monospace labels, no logo tiles) and must not read as a research publication. Google Sans is pinned by the owner.
keyCharacteristics: One drawing vocabulary: an olive area outlined at 2px, and square white corners with an ink border.
Olive works, light orange marks. Ink does everything else.
Beige ground on every screen; the close alone is ink.
Maps are drawn from open data in the page's own colours, unlabelled, and fade into the paper or sit in a hairline frame.
One typeface, Google Sans; hierarchy by weight and size, never by case or a second face.
Flat surfaces divided by 1px hairlines; one soft ink shadow, kept for things that lie on top.
Every figure is tabular and exact; a stale figure steps back in colour, it never disappears.

Motion is one authored moment per surface, drawn the way the thing would be drawn; the first screen's picture alone runs on by itself, and can be paused. Under reduced motion everything is simply there.

rules.name: The Olive Works, Orange Marks Rule
rules.body: Olive is for what the visitor does or has drawn; light orange is for what is counted and what is the brand's. Neither does the other's job, and neither is used as decoration.

rules.name: The Beige Ground Rule
rules.body: Every screen the visitor works on is the beige ground. A screen does not open on ink, on a tinted wash or on a picture with a frame of its own colour.

rules.name: The Ring Rule
rules.body: A pale orange never stands alone on a pale ground. A listing dot and a booked night wear the `occ-ring`; the mark sits inside an ink line.

rules.name: The Step Back Rule
rules.body: A figure that no longer describes the area on screen goes to `pending` until the new one arrives. It is never hidden, blurred or replaced by a spinner.

rules.name: The Turned Over Rule
rules.body: The close is the same palette inverted (`close` and `close-*`), not a second palette. The focus ring inverts with it.

rules.name: The Seven Sizes Rule
rules.body: Running type is 11, 13, 15, 16, 17 or 18px, plus the headline size. A new element takes one of them. The one exception is the first screen's sentence at 20px from 1024px.

rules.name: The Weight Not Case Rule
rules.body: A label is a sentence-case word at weight 600. There is no uppercase and no monospace anywhere, and tracking is never what makes something a label; the name of a body of water on a map is spaced out (0.08em) as maps do.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every surface that shows figures sets `tabular-nums`, and a figure's unit is smaller and muted beside it, never in a separate column.

rules.name: The Bold Twin Rule
rules.body: Where choosing an item makes it bolder (a tab, a contents entry), its bold setting is laid out invisibly under the regular one, so selecting moves nothing.

rules.name: The Card Is The Surface Rule
rules.body: Charts, tables, tabs and lists sit directly on their card, divided by hairlines. They do not get boxes of their own; the things that are boxed are objects in their own right (a sheet of paper, a message, a switch, a listing, a figure pinned to a map).

rules.name: The Lying On Top Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is a separate thing resting on what is under it": a sheet, a pinned card, a floating control, the field. Product cards, stage panels, filled buttons and bubbles are flat at rest and stay flat on hover.

rules.name: The Faded Edge Rule
rules.body: A map with no frame meets the paper by fading into it, with a mask on the drawing alone. What is drawn over the map (areas, corners, names, pinned cards) is on a sheet of its own and never fades.

rules.name: The Covered Card Rule
rules.body: A card under another recedes by scaling its body to 0.97 and taking a 6% veil of ink, driven by scroll. Its header row does neither, because it is still a working link.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: If it can be dragged, chosen, or stands for a point on a map, a line or a chart, it is a square with an ink border: white when empty, olive when hovered or held, ink when chosen, light orange when it is the thing being counted.

dos: Do draw anything new in the page's own hand: a 2px olive outline for an area, square nodes with an ink border, a 2px ink line for a chart or an icon, and at most one shape filled with the marking orange.
Do keep olive for what the visitor does or has drawn and light orange for what is counted or is the brand's.
Do keep the ground beige on every screen, and let a frameless map fade into it.
Do take every colour from a `--th-*` role, and mix a hairline from the card's own ground when the ground is tinted.
Do make a new map picture from open map data in the map colours recorded here, with no labels and no boundary lines of its own, and credit it on the page.
Do pin a figure to the place it describes: a white card with a one-pixel ink edge and the pinned shadow, joined to its area by an ink hairline, and say on the card what each figure is of.
Do set figures in tabular numerals at weight 600 with the unit beside them at 13px in muted, and say under each block what it covers.
Do send a stale figure to `pending` rather than hiding it, and leave out a figure that cannot be had rather than standing something in for it.
Do give every pressable thing a 44px target and a visible 2px focus ring, placed on the square itself for handles and sliders and round the whole field for the search.
Do put charts, tables and lists straight on the card, divided by hairlines.
Do make a new surface's one moment of motion the way the thing would be drawn, and leave everything in place under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use teal or tangerine; both were tried on this page and dropped by the owner.
Don't open a screen on a dark ground; a dark first screen was built and rejected. The close is the one ink surface, and it is the palette turned over.
Don't use the marking orange for text, for a button, or without an ink line or ring around it.
Don't add pill or badge labels, eyebrow lines above headings, monospace labels, uppercase or letter-spaced labels, or logo tiles.
Don't add a second typeface or a type size outside the seven.
Don't put a shadow on a product card, a stage panel, a filled button or a hover state; a shadow is for something lying on top of something else, as a control floating on a map is.
Don't round a handle or a node, and don't square a listing dot on a map of many listings.
Don't put a frame, a label layer or administrative boundaries on a generated map picture.

Don't use a gradient as decoration; the only gradients are the fade at the edge of something that scrolls or of a frameless map, the slider's two-colour track, and the ink hatching that means "blocked".
Don't let a figure count up, flash or animate on the cards; it shows its true value throughout.
Don't invent testimonials, client names, prices or plan contents.
